summary.headline: Blue Star Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 1.3% to Rs 4,072 Cr, a record quarter, with EBITDA margin up to 8%; management guides FY27 UCP margin to 8-8.5% despite cost pressure.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue grew 1.3% YoY to Rs 4,072 Cr, the highest ever quarterly revenue, and EBITDA excluding other income rose to Rs 326.3 Cr (8% margin vs 7% a year ago). FY26 revenue grew 3.6% to Rs 12,402 Cr while net profit fell to Rs 527.3 Cr from Rs 591.3 Cr, with the Labour Code gratuity and leave encashment charge taken as an exceptional item. Summer demand set in only from 13 April 2026, so channel inventory and the timing of the 13% price increase are the main near-term swing factors. Management said FY27 margins will be under pressure from raw material and petrochemical costs, and it declined to give FY27 revenue growth guidance.

segments.name: Segment 1: Electromechanical Projects and Commercial Air Conditioning
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue rose 1.1% to Rs 1,989.9 Cr with segment result of Rs 128.5 Cr (6.5% margin vs 7.6%). FY26 revenue grew 12.8% to Rs 6,762.8 Cr, but FY26 margin was 7.4% vs 8.2%; Q4 order inflow rose 35.7% to Rs 1,954.4 Cr while the EM projects order book fell to Rs 4,664.5 Cr from Rs 4,755.2 Cr.

segments.name: Segment 2: Unitary Cooling Products (RAC and commercial refrigeration)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue rose 1.3% to Rs 1,985 Cr with segment result of Rs 206.9 Cr (10.4% margin vs 8.4%). FY26 revenue fell 5.1% to Rs 5,332.4 Cr and segment result fell to Rs 434.8 Cr (8.2% margin vs 8.4%).

segments.name: Segment 3: Industrial, MedTech and Data Security Solutions
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue rose 7.3% to Rs 97.18 Cr with segment result of Rs 14.3 Cr (14.7% margin). FY26 revenue fell 12% to Rs 306.8 Cr, though margin improved to 11.4% from 8.5%; MedTech slowed on unresolved regulation while Industrial Solutions grew.

guidance_outlook: Segment 2 (UCP) EBIT margin target of 8% to 8.5% for FY27, with 8.5% to 9% possible in a good summer; management reiterated this as its outlook for this financial year.
Management expects margin pressure through FY27 from commodity, copper, petrochemical (styrene, polystyrene) and FX costs; it said margins will be under pressure until 2030 as the market expands.

Price increase of about 13% warranted: about 8% realised to date and roughly 5% more to come in May-June billings. The 13% covers the desired margins but excludes further post-war input cost increases.
Segment 1 (projects and commercial AC) margin target of 7% to 7.5%; commercial AC growth outlook of 8% to 10% for FY27, with data centre MEP revenue potentially more than doubling in about 3 years.
Annual capex of about Rs 250 to 350 Cr including maintenance, R&D and IT. Decision on one more RAC assembly line expected by October 2026.
Management said it was too early to guide FY27 revenue growth; it is cautiously optimistic and depends on how the summer plays out.
capex_capacity: Sri City RAC capacity is added in modules of 3 lakh units (3 to 6 to 9 lakh, with 12 lakh possible); Himachal plant runs at 100% of about 6.5 lakh units; Sri City plus outsourced units total about 9 lakh units.
Management said RAC and commercial refrigeration plants are operating close to 100% capacity this year if growth is good.
A further assembly line investment, deferred from last year, will be decided by October 2026; the building is already available.
Annual capex guidance of Rs 250 to 350 Cr covering maintenance, R&D, product development and IT.
Data centre CDU and fan-wall cooling are not in-house; the company has a few chillers and is seeking partners for CDUs with nothing material signed yet.
demand_pricing: Summer set in around 13 April 2026, with secondary sales picking up from the second week of April; management said it is not celebrating like 2024 and needs 2-3 more weeks to judge.
Dealer channel inventory is estimated at about 45 to 60 days, which management expects to clear within about 20 days if summer stays active.
Industry RAC volume is estimated at about 14.5 to 14.75 million units in FY26 (down about 5%); Blue Star's volume share is about 11.25% and value share about 14.25%, targeting 15%.
Management expects Q1 industry growth of about 25% to 30% in a good summer, with about 10% from price increases.
Management said consumer demand may soften if fuel prices rise, but the net 3% price increase after GST cut is unlikely to deter buyers.

Commercial AC demand driven by manufacturing (semiconductor, EV battery, solar) and data centres; office, education and IT bookings remain subdued. Commercial refrigeration is muted, with frozen food and QSR weak; storage water coolers grew double digits.
International: US business is at an early stage under a contract manufacturing model and depends on the India-US trade deal; Europe supplies began, with heat pump demand emerging.

qa_highlights.question: How much price increase has been taken since January including the BEE norm change, and how much more is needed?
qa_highlights.answer: About 5% from the energy label change and about 8% in total including raw material and FX; about 8% of a warranted 13% has been realised, with roughly 5% more coming in May-June billings.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company see margin pressure in Q1 from the price increase timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margin pressure will persist through the year; the extra price increase took effect in May, and 8% to 8.5% UCP margin remains the outlook for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the inventory level in RACs compared with January, and will price hikes cause demand destruction?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory is reasonable at about 45 to 60 days; management does not expect a sharp demand drop from the net 3% increase, but a fuel price shock could hit sentiment.

qa_highlights.question: Why are project margins stuck at 7% to 7.5% despite data centre growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Projects are a blended business (buildings, infra, factories, data centres); margins have run at 7% to 7.5% and management will not commit to 8% to 8.5% yet.

qa_highlights.question: What were Q4 margins affected by, and was there a provision reversal?
qa_highlights.answer: The Rs 17.5 Cr labour code provision reversal was in exceptional items and does not affect segment results.

qa_highlights.question: What is the data centre MEP market and order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Market estimated at about Rs 3,500 to 4,000 Cr; Blue Star's MEP business is about Rs 1,000 Cr a year with an order book of about Rs 1,500 Cr at any time. Equipment content is minimal, mainly electrical and mechanical items.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation from the war (copper, styrene, polystyrene, FX) may outpace further price increases, squeezing UCP margins below the 8% to 8.5% target.
Summer length: management needs active heat through mid-June, and a delayed monsoon could affect Q1 primary sales and secondary sales of RAC.
Consumer sentiment could weaken if fuel or diesel prices rise, and the price increase could push buyers down-market.
Projects: Rs 4,664.5 Cr order book fell year on year and FY26 order inflow was down 10%; Q4 margin dropped to 6.5%.
International: US demand is expected to decline and tariffs are unresolved; Europe is still slow.
Trade-war-related supply disruptions for raw materials, in both availability and prices.
key_quotes: We have been waiting for the summer season to take off in a big way, which indeed happened on 13th of April.
In one single sentence, we are happy that the summer season has set in, we are not celebrating like it was 2024 summer.
13% will cover the desired margin levels.
I will not, at this juncture say that it's going to become some 8% to 8.5% or 8.9%.
We remain cautiously optimistic about the prospects for FY27.
summary.management_tone: Management sounded confident about the summer demand recovery and the 13% price increase, but cautious on FY27: it declined to guide FY27 revenue growth, said margins will stay under pressure from commodity, petrochemical and FX costs, and said it is too early to judge the summer. It was evasive on the project margin uplift (not committing to 8% to 8.5%) and on international business, calling it a wrong time to talk long term.

adds.what: One more RAC assembly line (decision pending; building already available)

growth.why: Management declined to guide FY27 revenue growth ("too early"), only guiding segment margins (UCP 8-8.5%, projects 7-7.5%) and commercial AC growth of 8-10%; the UCP plant is at 100% utilisation, but the next RAC line is deferred to an October 2026 decision, so capacity relief is not yet committed.
